calls.head: The Senators will send their checkers at Stenberg
calls.body: At home, the Senators keep sending Pinto’s line (Cousins, Pinto and Amadio) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Travis Green has been using this group as a checking line on opponents’ second lines. Tonight the Sharks’ second line is Stenberg, Misa and Sherwood.

surprises.head: Yaroslav Askarov stole one
surprises.body: Askarov allowed 2 goals on 43 shots, worth 4.8 expected goals: 2.9 fewer than expected. That is more than San Jose’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 50 starts.

story.head: Askarov stands on his head
paras: Tim Stützle opened the scoring for the Senators early in the first, but Nolan Allan made it 1-1 for San Jose less than five minutes later. The Sharks’ Igor Chernyshov left late in the period and didn’t return. Tyler Toffoli, Collin Graf and Jacob Trouba scored three goals in just over four minutes midway through the second to put the Sharks up 4-1. Jordan Spence cut San Jose’s lead to 4-2 early in the third. Zack Ostapchuk added an empty-net goal with three and a half minutes left to make it 5-2. Ivar Stenberg added an empty-net goal with 17 seconds left to make it 6-2.

The score flatters the Sharks: the Senators had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Senators win about seven in ten. Yaroslav Askarov was the difference, stopping 41 of 43. Samuel Ersson stopped 22 of 26 for the Senators.
The Senators hit two posts and the crossbar, and the bounces never came. The Sharks improved to 6-4-1, and the Sens fell to 7-4-0.
